scope: Additional safe classroom experiment concepts only.

experiments.title: Citric acid and bicarbonate review
experiments.focus: Review the idea that acids and bicarbonates can produce a visible gas-forming change in the classroom model.
student_observations: The mixture changes visibly in the model.
Bubbles are a sign that a new gas is being formed conceptually.
Acids and carbonates/bicarbonates are useful for comparison lessons.
experiments.teacher_note: Keep the activity conceptual and classroom-level.

experiments.title: Magnesium carbonate and acid concept
experiments.focus: Connect a carbonate solid with an acid in a safe comparison model.
student_observations: The solid reacts in the model.
Small bubbles may appear as a sign of gas formation.
Carbonates can behave similarly in acid lessons.
experiments.teacher_note: Use this as a comparison with sodium bicarbonate and calcium carbonate.

experiments.title: Magnesium carbonate mixture
experiments.focus: Show that not every solid makes a clear solution in water.
student_observations: The solid does not disappear completely.
The liquid can look cloudy in the model.
Mixtures and solutions are not always the same thing.
experiments.teacher_note: A useful contrast with sugar and salt dissolving.

experiments.title: Acid-carbonate family comparison
experiments.focus: Compare two carbonate-related solids in the same lesson structure.
student_observations: Different solids can show different rates of visible change.
All members of the family can be discussed using the same idea.
experiments.teacher_note: Good wrap-up activity for acids, carbonates, and observation skills.
